teacherEmulator.title: Try it yourself — a practice copy of Edura
teacherEmulator.missHint: Not that one — look for the control with the indigo outline and press it.
teacherEmulator.finishedBody: You can now read your day, price a class, take attendance and fix an “at the centre, not in the lesson” row, close a lesson so your share lands, and request a payout. Your real account works exactly the same way.
teacherEmulator.sandboxNote: Everything above is practice — the data and prices are invented, no real money moves and nothing is recorded on your account. The real platform and centre shares appear on your own screen before any closing.

firstRun.title: First time here? Take 3 minutes
firstRun.body: Before you open your account, let's walk through a practice copy step by step: price a class, take attendance, close the lesson so your money lands, and request a payout. No real data changes.

screens.pricedHint: The price is fixed on the class and is what the counter charges. Changing it later does not re-price past lessons.
screens.unpricedBody: This class has no monthly or per-session price yet — students cannot subscribe, and its lessons cannot be closed or distributed.
screens.counterOnly: At the centre, not in the lesson
screens.settleTitle: Close the lesson and distribute it
screens.settledBody: This lesson was already closed and distributed, and your share was credited to your wallet. It cannot be closed again and its distribution cannot be edited.
screens.blockedNoAttendance: No attendance is saved yet. This card reads saved attendance, so save it first.
screens.blockedUnpriced: This class has no price, so the lesson would distribute nothing. Set the class pricing first.
screens.blockedNoPresent: No students are marked present, so there is nothing to distribute. Take attendance first.
screens.settleAction: Close the lesson and distribute EGP {amount} across {n} students
screens.settleHint: The distribution is written to the ledger once, and cannot be undone.
screens.settleArmedHint: Written to the ledger in your name, and credited to the teacher's and the center's wallets immediately.
screens.nothingAvailable: Nothing available — funds are reserved by open requests or the balance is empty.
screens.withdrawArmedHint: A request cannot be cancelled once sent.
screens.counterOnlyHint: They paid and entered the centre but never reached the lesson. Not counted present until you decide.

welcome.title: Welcome — this is entirely a practice copy
welcome.body: The screens ahead are exactly yours, with invented data: one class, six students, and today's lesson. Press “Got it” and let's go.

classesToday.title: The four numbers you open on every day
classesToday.body: Classes today, pending grades, total students, attendance rate. That is everything you need in the first thirty seconds.

pendingGrades.title: “Pending Grades” is a workload figure, not a statistic
pendingGrades.body: It is the one number parents experience as lateness on your part. Make ending the week at zero your target.

todaySchedule.title: Today's schedule
todaySchedule.body: The lesson's time, room and status. If the room reads “TBD”, check with the centre before the lesson.

openClass.title: Open the class
openClass.body: Press the class card to see its detail.

unpriced.title: This is the commonest thing that traps a new teacher
unpriced.body: This class has no price. Which means: no student can subscribe, and — more importantly — its lessons cannot be closed and will distribute no money at all. Classes created by accepting a centre collaboration always start this way.

setPrice.title: Price it
setPrice.body: Press the button to set the lesson price.

priced.title: Now it works
priced.body: Students can subscribe, the counter can collect, and the lesson has become closable.

pickLesson.title: Open today's lesson
pickLesson.body: Press today's lesson. Note the one above it marked “Completed” — that one is already closed.

roster.title: The six students
roster.body: Everyone arrives as “Present” by default and you change what needs changing. The three controls on the right sit in the same place for every student.

markAbsent.title: Mark an absence
markAbsent.body: Salma is not here today — press the absent control in her row.

counterOnly.title: Look at Mariam — this is the row that costs you money
counterOnly.body: Mariam paid and passed the counter, but nobody confirmed her at the classroom door, so her state is “At the centre, not in the lesson”. She is not counted present and will not enter the distribution — your share shrinks while she has paid.

fixCounterOnly.title: Fix it yourself
fixCounterOnly.body: If Mariam really is in the room, press “Present” in her row.

save.title: Save
save.body: Press “Save attendance”. The closing card reads what is saved, not what is on screen.

settleCard.title: This card is what pays you
settleCard.body: A student's payment alone does not credit your share — closing does. Nobody closes the lesson for you, and no nightly job closes it either.

readShares.title: Read the figures before you press
readShares.body: Your share, the centre's and the platform's, per attending student. Add them up — they must equal the lesson price exactly. These figures are practice ones; the real rates are set by the platform and shown here before every closing.

pressSettle.title: The button carries the amount itself
pressSettle.body: Not “confirm” on a figure you never read — the button tells you how much, across how many students. Press it.

confirmSettle.title: A second confirmation, on purpose
confirmSettle.body: The distribution is written to the ledger once and cannot be undone. Press “Final confirmation”.

settled.title: Your share is credited
settled.body: The lesson is “Completed” and the amount is in your wallet. No second closing for the same lesson, and no editing the distribution — a correction, if ever needed, is a new opposite entry.

onceOnly.title: Make it a habit
onceOnly.body: Close every lesson while you are still in the room, right after saving attendance. A pile-up of open lessons is the commonest cause of an empty wallet.

balance.title: Three numbers, not one
balance.body: “Wallet balance” is everything owed to you, “Available to withdraw” is what you can request today, and “Reserved by open requests” is a payout not yet paid.

withdraw.title: Request a payout
withdraw.body: Press “Withdraw earnings” — leaving the amount empty means withdrawing the whole balance.

reserved.title: Look at the numbers now
reserved.body: “Available to withdraw” dropped to zero and “Wallet balance” did not move. That difference is reserved by your request, not lost — and it is the pair teachers misread most.

requests.title: Track it from here
requests.body: The status moves: “Pending” → “Approved” → “Paid”. And if it is rejected, the reason is in the “Note” column and the amount returns to available.

done.title: You have walked the whole path
done.body: You priced, took attendance, fixed a counter-only row, closed a lesson and requested a payout. Press “Got it” to finish.

withdrawConfirm.title: Then confirm again
withdrawConfirm.body: The button names the amount and waits for a second press. That is deliberate: a request cannot be cancelled once sent.

teacherTour.title: A quick tour of Edura
teacherTour.moreHint: On a phone: press “More” first — it's inside there.

welcome.title: Welcome to Edura 👋
welcome.body: This tour shows you the things you'll actually do — and it won't just say “this is your wallet”, it will show you how, step by step. It's ordered by what costs you money if you don't know it. You can skip at any point.

priceClass.title: First: make sure your group has a price
priceClass.body: A group with no price cannot be subscribed to, and its lessons refuse to close — so you will not be paid a piastre for them.

how.1: Open "Groups" from the menu and pick the group
how.2: If it warns that the group has no price, it needs pricing
how.3: Your own group (no centre): the price is set when you create it, and there is no screen to change it afterwards yet — contact us and we will set it
how.4: A group from a centre: **the centre** sets the price — ask them to

priceClass.note: The price is not editable from the classes screen after creation. A group created by accepting a centre's collaboration request starts at zero, and the centre is who prices it.

attendance.title: How to take attendance
attendance.body: This is what decides who counts when the lesson's revenue is distributed.

how.2: Pick the lesson — every row names the group and the hall, not just the time
how.3: Anyone "at the centre, not in the lesson" sits in a box above the register — mark them present or absent
how.4: Mark the rest present / absent / excused, then "Save attendance"

attendance.note: If a student shows as “at the centre — did not attend the lesson”, they checked in at the counter but never entered the hall. That is not attendance and does not count in the distribution — even if they paid.

closeLesson.title: Then close the lesson — this is what pays you
closeLesson.body: Distribution does not happen by itself. A lesson you never close puts nothing in your wallet.

how.1: After saving attendance, scroll to the "Close the lesson" card under the register
how.2: The button names the amount and the number of students before you press it
how.3: Check the teacher, centre and platform shares

closeLesson.note: The distribution is written to the ledger once and cannot be undone. A closed lesson cannot be closed again.

door.title: If you use counter + door mode
door.body: There are two attendance modes and you choose. In the two-check-in mode a second check-in happens at the hall door.

how.3: Ask for the student's code or scan their card

door.note: You can change the mode in Settings → attendance mode. In “counter only” mode the counter check-in alone is enough.

wallet.title: Your wallet and withdrawing earnings
wallet.body: Where you see what you have earned, and ask for it. It is in the bar now.

how.2: Read "Wallet balance" and "Available" — the gap between them is held by open requests
how.3: Press "Withdraw", and type an amount or leave it empty to take everything
how.4: The button names the amount — press once to arm it, again to send. There is no cancel afterwards

wallet.note: “Available to withdraw” is not the same as “Wallet balance”: any open request reserves its amount until it is settled. If available looks low, you probably have a request still in flight.

grades.title: How to record grades
grades.body: Grades are not worked out for you — you enter them, and the student and their parent see them immediately.

how.3: Add an assessment and set its maximum score
how.4: Enter the students' marks and save

materials.title: How to upload a handout
materials.body: What you upload here reaches that group's students only.

how.3: Upload the file and give it a clear name

centers.title: How to work with a centre
centers.body: Collaboration starts as a request from either side, and accepting is what creates the group and its schedule.

how.2: The centres you already work with are at the top, collaboration requests below them
how.3: Check the subject, year, hall, times and share

centers.note: Accepting creates the group and the schedule immediately. Check the centre's share before you accept — it comes out of every lesson's revenue.

team.title: How to add an assistant
team.body: An assistant does everything you do except money, and every action is recorded as theirs “on behalf of” you.

how.2: Press add assistant, enter their name and email, and send the invite
how.3: They set their own password from the link
how.4: At the bottom of the page is a panel saying exactly what an assistant can do — and which doors are shut to them (your wallet, payouts, prices, assistants)

team.note: An assistant cannot reach your wallet, request a payout, or add other assistants. Everything they do is logged on your behalf.

messages.title: How to message students and parents
messages.body: You can write to your students, their parents and centre staff.

how.3: Pick the name from the list

messages.note: If the student is under 18, their parent can read the conversation — and a clear notice appears to both sides saying so.

practice.title: And if you'd rather try it first
practice.body: There's a full practice copy you can rehearse on without touching anything real.

how.2: It walks you through it: price a group, take attendance, close a lesson, request a payout
how.3: All the data is invented and no money moves

finish.title: That's it — your turn 🎉
finish.body: The tour is done. If any group has no price, sort that first — without it there are no subscriptions, no closing, and no money. And if you'd rather rehearse, “Practice” is in the menu.
